hints: Resolve forces in horizontal and vertical directions, using the equilibrium conditions $\Sigma F_x = 0$ and $\Sigma F_y = 0$.
Form the horizontal equation $F\cos\theta + 10 - 40\cos 60^\circ = 0$ to find $F\cos\theta = 10\text{ N}$.
Form the vertical equation $F\sin\theta + 40\sin 60^\circ - 50 = 0$ to find $F\sin\theta = 50 - 20\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.
Divide the two components to find $\tan\theta = 1.5359$, then use Pythagoras to determine the magnitude $F$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium ($\Sigma F_x = 0$):
$$F\cos\theta + 10 - 40\cos 60^\circ = 0$$
$$F\cos\theta = 40(0.5) - 10 = 20 - 10 = 10\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium ($\Sigma F_y = 0$):
$$F\sin\theta + 40\sin 60^\circ - 50 = 0$$
$$F\sin\theta = 50 - 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 50 - 20\sqrt{3} \approx 15.359\text{ N}$$

Divide the two component equations to find $\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{F\sin\theta}{F\cos\theta} = \frac{15.359}{10} = 1.5359$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(1.5359) \approx 56.9^\circ$$

Calculate the magnitude $F$ using Pythagoras' theorem:
$$F = \sqrt{(F\cos\theta)^2 + (F\sin\theta)^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + 15.359^2}$$
$$F = \sqrt{100 + 235.899} = \sqrt{335.899} \approx 18.3\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the conditions for the equilibrium of coplanar forces acting at a point:
$$\sum F_x = 0\quad\text{and}\quad\sum F_y = 0$$

Resolve forces horizontally (taking the positive $x$-direction as to the right):
$$F\cos\theta + 10 - 40\cos 60^\circ = 0$$
$$\cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \implies 40\cos 60^\circ = 20$$
$$F\cos\theta + 10 - 20 = 0$$
$$F\cos\theta = 10\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically (taking the positive $y$-direction as upwards):
$$F\sin\theta + 40\sin 60^\circ - 50 = 0$$
$$\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \implies 40\sin 60^\circ = 20\sqrt{3}$$
$$F\sin\theta = 50 - 20\sqrt{3} \approx 50 - 34.6410 = 15.3590\text{ N}$$

Divide the vertical component by the horizontal component to eliminate $F$ and solve for $\theta$:
$$\frac{F\sin\theta}{F\cos\theta} = \tan\theta = \frac{15.3590}{10} = 1.5359$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(1.5359) \approx 56.932^\circ$$
$$\theta = 56.9^\circ\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$

Use the Pythagorean identity $F^2 = (F\cos\theta)^2 + (F\sin\theta)^2$ to find the magnitude $F$:
$$F = \sqrt{(10)^2 + (15.3590)^2}$$
$$10^2 = 100$$
$$(15.3590)^2 \approx 235.8989$$
$$F = \sqrt{100 + 235.8989} = \sqrt{335.8989} \approx 18.3275\text{ N}$$
$$F = 18.3\text{ N}\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$

hints: Calculate the horizontal and vertical components of the resultant force using $F = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 45^\circ$.
Note that the horizontal component vanishes: $10\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ + 10 - 40\cos 60^\circ = 10 + 10 - 20 = 0$.
Evaluate the vertical component $10 + 20\sqrt{3} - 50 = 20\sqrt{3} - 40$, noting it is negative, so state the magnitude as positive $40 - 20\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ downwards.
walkthrough:
Resolve horizontally to find the horizontal component of the resultant $R_x$:
$$R_x = 10\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ + 10 - 40\cos 60^\circ$$
$$R_x = 10\sqrt{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) + 10 - 40(0.5) = 10 + 10 - 20 = 0\text{ N}$$

Resolve vertically to find the vertical component of the resultant $R_y$:
$$R_y = 10\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ + 40\sin 60^\circ - 50$$
$$R_y = 10 + 20\sqrt{3} - 50 = 20\sqrt{3} - 40\text{ N}$$

Since $20\sqrt{3} - 40 < 0$, the resultant acts vertically downwards with exact positive magnitude:
$$\text{Magnitude} = 40 - 20\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Direction: in the direction of the } 50\text{ N force (vertically downwards)}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Name the method: find the resultant vector by resolving all forces into horizontal and vertical components, $R = (R_x, R_y)$.

Calculate the horizontal component $R_x$ using $F = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 45^\circ$:
$$R_x = 10\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ + 10 - 40\cos 60^\circ$$
$$10\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ = 10\sqrt{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 10$$
$$40\cos 60^\circ = 40(0.5) = 20$$
$$R_x = 10 + 10 - 20 = 0\text{ N}$$

Since $R_x = 0$, the resultant force acts purely in the vertical direction. Now calculate the vertical component $R_y$ (taking upwards as positive):
$$R_y = 10\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ + 40\sin 60^\circ - 50$$
$$10\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ = 10\sqrt{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 10$$
$$40\sin 60^\circ = 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 20\sqrt{3}$$
$$R_y = 10 + 20\sqrt{3} - 50 = 20\sqrt{3} - 40\text{ N}$$

Evaluate the sign of $R_y$: since $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732$, $20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.64 < 40$. Therefore, $R_y$ is negative, which means the resultant acts vertically downwards (in the direction of the $50\text{ N}$ force).

Express the magnitude as a strictly positive exact quantity:
$$\text{Magnitude} = |R_y| = -(20\sqrt{3} - 40) = 40 - 20\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Direction: vertically downwards (in the direction of the } 50\text{ N force)}$$
